partners.mechanism_chain: Glycogen Synthase 1 (HGNC:4552) —DISRUPTS→ Disrupted Glycogen Synthesis; Disrupted Glycogen Synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal Glycogen Levels; Abnormal Glycogen Levels —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001347); Phosphoglucomutase 1 (HGNC:9173) —DISRUPTS→ Disrupted Glycogenolysis; Disrupted Glycogenolysis —LEADS_TO→ Glucose-1-phosphate deficiency; Glucose-1-phosphate deficiency —LEADS_TO→ UDP-glucose deficiency; UDP-glucose deficiency —LEADS_TO→ Disrupted Glycosylation; Disrupted Glycosylation —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Abnormal Glycogen Levels —LEADS_TO→ Disrupted Glycosylation. Loss-of-function mutations in GYS1 impair glycogen synthesis, leading to abnormal glycogen levels and downstream effects that contribute to phenotypes like muscle weakness. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in PGM1 disrupt glycogenolysis, causing deficiencies in glucose-1-phosphate and subsequently UDP-glucose. This UDP-glucose deficiency directly impairs cellular glycosylation, a critical process for protein function, leading to phenotypes such as seizures. The convergence occurs at the level of cellular glycosylation, which is affected by both abnormal glycogen metabolism and the direct deficiency in UDP-glucose.
